source_caption:
🎬 Draft Day (2014)

Draft Day follows Sonny Weaver Jr., the general manager of the Cleveland Browns, as he faces one of the most important and stressful days of his professional career during the NFL Draft. With the future of the struggling football franchise hanging in the balance, Sonny must make decisions that could completely change the team’s direction. Under enormous pressure from the team’s owner, coaching staff, fans, and sports media, he unexpectedly trades away valuable future draft picks to secure the number-one overall selection. However, as the hours count down toward the draft, Sonny begins questioning whether the highly regarded quarterback everyone expects him to choose is truly the right player for the team. While evaluating talented prospects, negotiating risky trades, and uncovering surprising information, he also struggles with personal challenges involving his family and his relationship with the team’s salary-cap analyst, Ali Parker. As competing teams attempt to take advantage of his situation, Sonny must trust his instincts and find a way to build a winning future without sacrificing everything the Browns have worked toward. Combining intense sports drama, behind-the-scenes NFL negotiations, emotional conflicts, and unexpected twists, the film explores leadership, ambition, pressure, loyalty, and the difficult decisions that can define an entire career.

🎭 Genre: Sports • Drama

⭐ IMDb: 6.8/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 50m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Ivan Reitman

source_details.synopsis: Draft Day is a 2014 American sports drama film directed by Ivan Reitman, and starring Kevin Costner and Jennifer Garner, with Denis Leary, Frank Langella, Sam Elliott, Ellen Burstyn and Chadwick Boseman in supporting roles. The premise revolves around the fictional general manager of the Cleveland Browns (Costner) deciding what to do after his team acquires the number one draft pick in the upcoming National Football League draft. The film premiered in Los Angeles on April 7, 2014 and was released in the United States by Summit Entertainment (through Lionsgate) on April 11, 2014. It received mixed reviews from critics and was a box office failure, grossing only $29 million against its $25 mil
